Can a 17th Century Samurai Teach us about life?

I was walking and listening to a podcast when the guest quoted a poem.
​
I came to a full stop. Rewound and listened again. And again. And again.
​
I've since read this over and over and shared it with a few friends.
​
This is a translation of a haiku by Mizuta Masahide (水田 正秀, 1657–1723). Masahide was a samurai turned poet. Not much is known about him, but he left us with this gift:
​
"My barn having burned to the ground,
I can now see the moon more completely."
​
The end, with it's pain and loss, unlocks new places inside you.
​
May we have the courage to embrace the endings and find what good may come on the other side.

Have you ever felt like you had more to give but didn’t know what to do about it?

Have you ever felt like your life and work were stuck on repeat uncertain of how to move forward?

We often end up in places like these.

Life asks a lot of us. We have responsibilities that pull us in multiple directions. We have people who ask us to be certain things in all the different contexts that we move between — work, home, family, etc.

We lose track of what brings us joy and makes us come alive.

I remember being a kid and feeling like everything was possible. If you asked me at 12 what I wanted to be I would have told you a number of things: an astronaut, DNA scientist, a rock star, and on and on.

Everything was possible.

But everything is not possible. Not anymore at least.

And while that can be very discouraging, there’s good news.

While not EVERYTHING may be possible, SOMETHING is possible.

Something more. Something better. Something that makes a difference for you and for the world.

This is what the Calling Course helps you identify, articulate, and pursue.

💡 An Idea

You Don't Need a Why

❌ You don’t need a why...
​
We hear all the time how important it is to have a clear “why” in your life and business.
​
🧐 But have you ever thought about WHY you need a why?
​
Yes, I know the answer:
✔️ So you’ll be able to recall it when things are hard
✔️ So you can make sure all the decisions you’re making are taking you to in the right direction.
✔️ Etc.
​
Those are all fine. And I drank that kool-aid for a long time on all of that.
​
But here’s the problem:
IF what you’re doing is so personally challenging and painful that you have to remind yourself WHY you’re doing it, then you have a problem.
​
Most entrepreneurs don’t have a WHY problem. We have a HOW problem.
​
❌ If your pace is unsustainable, clarifying your why won’t help.
​
❌ If you’re over-working yourself, knowing WHY isn’t going keep you healthy.
​
❌ If you’re making less money than you need to be, spending more time than you want to be, and experiencing more stress than you should be — your why isn’t going to help.
​
Change your “how”.
​
✅ How you live your days is how you live your life.
​
I’ve burned out hard on this path, and I know from experience that when how you’re building your business and pursuing your goals is fun and balanced, the why takes care of itself.
​
Stop sacrificing yourself to a life you don't love in order to gain a future that may never come.
​
If you're with me, tell me in the comments. I want to know that I'm not the only one.
​
And if you need help course correcting your entrepreneurial path, I'm here for you.
​

💡 An Idea:

Surrendering the Dream

I've been thinking how much we idealize what could be in life. This applies to so much: careers, relationships, creative pursuits, parenting, etc.

No matter how hard we try though, what we get in life is never the ideal. This can be both disappointing and liberating.

There's much to be gained by holding on to our dreams loosely and chasing after them, while also letting go of the specifics.

We must make room for the details to be different from the dream.

It can be helpful to feel disappointed by this gap. It's only by feeling the disappointment that you're able to accept your current reality for what it is.

Maybe you don't have the perfect job, spouse, child, life, etc. But what you have may be very good.

In fact, what you have may even be better than what you wanted — if you have the eyes to see it.

I hope you'll have the courage to do so.

No. The course is not faith based. You do not need to hold a specific system for it to work. broadcasts.subject: Transformational moments [+ workshop replay]
broadcasts.content:
Hi Friends,

A few days ago I hosted a new workshop called How to Avoid a Career Crisis. If you were one of the folks who joined live, THANK YOU! I had a blast! I’m still feeling so energized by the experience!

If you weren’t able to join, no worries! Here is the replay link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2VPRcxoXa_Q​

As I shared in the training, career and life crisis are incredibly human and normal experience — even though they usually don’t feel like it.

We don’t talk about them enough when we’re in them.

It makes sense though. We all feel this pressure to have it all together and have it all figured out. And the essence of these transitional moments in life is that you don’t have it figured out.

But I’m here to say: that’s ok! It’s great in fact!

How can I say that? Because the moment you let yourself not have it all figured out is the moment you open yourself up to receive what is emerging in your life and become who you are being called to be.

I use that word, “called” loosely — because it can have a lot of baggage. I’m not talking about some mystical permanent ball and chain calling that you must bear. Instead, I’m talking about you becoming more fully who you are. You letting your identity guide you and living into the best possible version of yourself in the world.

This is why I get so fired up about career and life crises! They’re such powerful moments in our lives that are just teeming with latent potential. They’re an opportunity to grab ahold of your life, take it by the horns, and make it into a life you love passionately.

How amazing would that be?

Or, let me reframe that for us: how amazing WILL that be?

THIS is the stuff that gets me fired up. And this is why I was so excited to share this training with you.

This could change your life. I know it has changed mine.

I hope you’ll take some time to watch the training.

To your success,

-Dan

PS- Whether or not the Calling Course is right for you, I hope you'll watch this training. I believe it's some of the most important content that I've created recently: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2VPRcxoXa_Q​

We realize that the path we're on is no longer leading us to our desired destination.

In this week's issue we have: a big (and this time very personal) idea (*gulp*), a podcast, and a roundup of a few fun things (as usual).

Let's get into it!

Double or Nothing: a Confession

*Deep breath... This next part is tough.*

When you get close to your work in the world — not your job, but the work you were made to do — there are a lot of ways that fear and self-sabotage can interfere.

I've been building the Meaning Movement online for 8 years. In that time, I've only spent a few years really focused on it.

Why? Oh, I can give you a million reasons to justify it. But the real reason is that I've been hiding.

I'm so afraid of going ALL IN on something that I care this much about.

I'm so afraid of putting too much of my heart and soul into something and have it land flat.

And there are stories behind this. I could tell you about failed attempts at launches and growth and how much they haunt me.

But I'll save those stories for another time.

The point is this (and I hate even writing it, but it's truth and needs to be said): I've been hiding from this work, trying to protect myself from past pain, and keeping it at arm's distance.

I believe, more than anything in the world, that you have something to say. You have a gift to give. And I want desperately to be a part of helping you find it, create it, and live into it.

It's a meta, but I know that is my work: helping you find and do yours.

AND YET, it's so much easier for me to keep busy, be "reasonable", play it safe, and keep myself distracted.

Over the past few months I've been realizing this. And I'm beginning the process of leaning in and facing those fears.

But there comes a time when you have to leap. For me, this is that moment. I'm going double or nothing. I'm investing myself, my energy, and any resources that I can muster into taking the Meaning Movement to a new place.

I'm terrified. But also excited.

And I can't do it alone.

Which is where you come in.

If you want to be a part of this journey with me, there are a few easy ways that I'd love to have your help. Reply to this email and I'll follow up with you there. Just say, "I'm in." And I'll respond back.

Thanks for reading. Thanks being a part of this.

With so much gratitude 🙏 🙏 🙏

Vanessa Van Edwards is a recovering awkward person and introvert who is on a mission to help everyone learn how to engage, interact, and lead with authenticity and genuine engagement. What that means is that she's teaching people how to interpret and use the many verbal and non-verbal cues that often go unnoticed so you can feel more at ease and in control of how you show up.

It's really fun stuff. I'm very into it. I've learned a lot from her that I'm already putting into practice.

Vanessa is the Lead Investigator at Science of People. She is the bestselling author of Captivate: The Science of Succeeding with People. More than 50 million people have watched her YouTube tutorials and TEDx Talk.

She works with entrepreneurs, growing businesses, and trillion-dollar companies; and has been featured all over the web.

More than anything, what I love about Vanessa is how she practices what she preaches. She's warm, engaging, and a fantastic communicator.

🎧 Listen in or read along here: themeaningmovement.com/vanessa 🎧

🥳 Throwing better parties! My friend and recent podcast guest, Nick Gray just released a book about throwing parties and it's on sale for $1.99 on kindle right now. It's practical, fun, and can be applied to just about any type of party you'd like to host. My wife and I have been using his method to throw cocktail parties. I used some of his technics at my birthday party. It's fantastic. I'd love for you to pick up a copy: https://amzn.to/3O179Np .

In fact, if you're in the pacific northwest and want to come to one of our parties, hit reply and let me know!

📚 A few fun books I'm reading:

As mentioned above, I'm doubling down on the Meaning Movement and as such, I'm having to face some fears, anxieties, trauma, and limiting beliefs. As I do, I've been reading some great books about mindset. While these might be a bit out there for some, they're hitting me right where I need it right now:

  • 📕 Breaking the Habit of Being Yourself: How to Lose Your Mind and Create a New One by Joe Dispenza - This book is part pop-psychology, part quantum physics, and part mindset. It's great and is helping me see how much I (still) limit my future by my beliefs about what's possible.
    ​
  • 📘 You Are a Badass at Making Money: Master the Mindset of Wealth by Jen Sincero - Much like the book above, this one helps you unpack all your thoughts, feelings, and fears about money, making money, and your self worth. Again, it's exactly what I need right now.

Pay attention to how much you might be complicating things in life. You'll be surprised.

How do you think about calling and vocation? When you think about those ideas in your life today, what form do they take?

When I interview creatives about their work, I often ask them how they think about the idea of voice and how they found their voices in their art and creativity.

But talking to artists about it is simply a shortcut.

It’s easy to talk to them about it because the arts have space for related ideas. If you’re an artist you recognize that you have a style. You must.

If you’re creating something that other interact with, you have to be intentional about your artistic perspective. Sometime you even need to write artist statements, where you have to articulate bits of all of this.

The challenge for the rest of us non-artists is that we still have a voice, yet our chosen fields give us less opportunities to think intentionally about it. Instead, it’s a concept that stirs something in us, yet leaves us uncertain how to engage with it.

I’d like to tackle this head on.

Everyone has a voice. YES! Even you! Not only that but your voice has everything to do with who you were made to be, what you were made to do, and how you find meaning, purpose, and fulfillment in your work.

Your voice is the narrative arch that holds your life and work story together.

I dive deep into this idea in the Calling Course, which is open for enrollment at our lowest ever available price for the next few days. Join here: thecallingcourse.com/new​

Whether or not you decide to join the course, I want to invite you to think about your work and your voice as an important part of what you bring to the world.

No matter your job and no matter your chosen career, your work is its best when you show up in it, with your voice and your full presence.

Sure. Not every workplace and work expression is going to accommodate this whole heatedly— but we all know when we’ve seen it and felt it.

There's a woman who works at the post office I typically go to who brings so much life to the room. She knows her customers by name. She's makes them smile. She laughs. She creates something meaningful in a job that is known for being dry and even soul-sucking.

She uses her voice. And it changes the world around her. You can't be around her and not notice.

So many of us have multiple passions that compete for time, attention, and resources — especially when it comes to our careers and work. So often we feel the need to choose one thing and leave behind all the rest in order to excel and succeed.

But what if you don't actually have to choose? What if you can be successful at more than one pursuit at that same time?

This is a question I often ask myself. If you've listened to the show for some time, you'll know that's true about me.

Culture tends to push us toward the myth that we can only do one thing to be successful. And while there is a trade off involved in multiple pursuits, there's also a synergy that can be present between projects.

Our guest today demonstrates that well. Calvin Nowell is both a singer and marketer. He pursues both in tandem as two parallel careers.
